search_surface: Debian popularity contest (popcon) source-package and binary-package installation counts; the C/C++ adoption source already used by scripts/snapshot_popcon.py

search.method: case-insensitive substring 'json' in Debian source-package names (sourcemax/by_inst); ordered by installations; all hits recorded

cpp_json_parser_classification.name: json-c
cpp_json_parser_classification.status: excluded: C library, belongs to the C cell

cpp_json_parser_classification.name: libjson-rpc-cpp
cpp_json_parser_classification.status: excluded: JSON-RPC framework built on JsonCpp

boost_json_binary_packages.note: All libboost-json* binary rows from the same binary_by_inst file (sha256 recorded under sources), re-read 2026-11-17 for the Boost.JSON pilot; the original binary_packages list omitted the libboost-json runtime rows. Boost.JSON has no JSON-specific Debian source package: boost1.83 sourcemax covers all Boost libraries. These binary counts are not the cell's primary sourcemax metric and are not ranked against it; libboost-json-dev is the separately labeled fallback.

multi_purpose_sources_with_json_modules.note: Counts of these sources cover whole frameworks (Qt Core with QJsonDocument, all of Boost, POCO); they are not JSON-specific and are not ranked against single-purpose JSON libraries. Boost.JSON and POCO JSON binary packages are listed in binary_packages.

secondary_signal_github_stars.note: Not the ranking metric. GitHub repository stars captured 2026-11-17T03:26:07Z from api.github.com/repos/<repo>; recorded because they disagree with popcon for nlohmann/json.
